title: Effects of spacing of item repetitions in continuous recognition memory: does item retrieval difficulty promote item retention in older adults?
authors: Aslı Kılıç, William J. Hoyer, Marc W. Howard
caption_short: Schematic of continuous word recognition with confidence: words appear one at a time, each up to three times, and after every word the participant rates from 1 (sure new) to 9 (sure old) whether it was seen before.
notes: Drawn by us: no open copy of the paper was found (not in PMC; the METU repository record and the Howard lab publication page carry no PDF), so we could not check for a task figure. The schematic follows the PubMed abstract (PMID 23607400: words presented once, twice or three times, confidence ratings) and the structure of the released OSF files (node wsu8h: five cycles of 315 trials per participant, ratings 1 to 9, repeat gaps from a few to more than a hundred trials). Example words and ratings are illustrative, not from the data.
